newsitem.title: GREECE: Riot police head to TVX Gold mine in Greece.
newsitem.headline: Riot police head to TVX Gold mine in Greece.

text.p: Riot police have been sent to the TVX Gold mines in northern Greece where local residents have blocked a main access road to stop work for 10 months, government and police sources told Reuters.
"The road will be opened within a few hours," a government official, who requested anonymity, told Reuters.
The decision to send riot police came a day after TVX Gold Hellas, the Greek subsidiary, said it would suspend all work and stop paying 650 workers next week if the main access road were not opened.
TVX paid $47 million last December for the mines near the northern city of Salonika. Greece said the deal represented a $270 million foreign investment -- the largest in 30 years.
But local residents have blocked the main access road from the outset, saying the environment and tourist industry would be hurt. The blockade has stopped heavy equipment from reaching the mines.
After the announcement by TVX Gold Hellas, Development Minister Vasso Papandreou said the government would ensure the mines could operate normally.

"The government will not give in. The government will honour its signature. It will not give in to the illegal acts of small interest groups which embarrass our country internationally," she said in a statement. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
